attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is applied with a non-anchored start to a URL match that can be arbitrarily long. For a long run of punctuation followed by a non-punctuation character, the engine retries from every start position, so cost is quadratic in run length. A stored description with a very long dotted or punctuated token would stall rendering of the item page for every neighbor who views it.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; ... ABSENT: any maximum length on item.description or on URL tokens in tokenize()

attacks.claim: Stripping a trailing ')' unconditionally breaks balanced-parenthesis URLs such as Wikipedia article links. The link is truncated to a 404 target and the ')' is rendered as plain text.
The stated invariant that truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens is contradicted by the code's mid-word fallback, which the test suite also asserts (400 'x' characters cut to 280).
attacks.evidence: "truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens" vs. "else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') });" and "expect(truncate(tokenize('x'.repeat(400)), 280).tokens).toEqual([{ kind: 'text', value: 'x'.repeat(280) }]);"

attacks.claim: The toggle uses aria-expanded while its visible label also changes between 'Show more' and 'Show less', which conveys the state twice and can confuse screen-reader users. Multiple identical 'Show more' buttons on a page have no item-specific accessible name.

Links that fall past the 280-character cut are hidden until the user expands the description. The motivating case, owners pasting product or manual links, is partly undercut because those links are not visible in the collapsed view.
attacks.evidence: {(expanded ? all : short.tokens).map(...)} ... ABSENT: any affordance or preview for links hidden by truncation

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is an unanchored-start regex with a trailing `+$` that backtracks quadratically on a long run of punctuation that is not at the end of the match. Any owner can write a description like `https://a` followed by 100k `!` and then a letter, which hangs the item page for every neighbor who views it. The description has no length cap.
Stripping a trailing `)` breaks URLs whose path legitimately ends in a closing parenthesis, such as Wikipedia-style links. The href is cut short and the link goes to the wrong page.

The PR claims truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens, but the fallback hard-cuts a text token mid-word when it has no whitespace in range. The fallback also ignores UTF-16 length by slicing code points, and a head that begins with whitespace (cut === 0) is dropped rather than handled.
attacks.evidence: else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') });

attacks.claim: A leading link is always shown in full, so a very long URL as the first token defeats the collapse on phones, which is the problem the PR is meant to solve.
attacks.evidence: out.push(t); // a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing

attacks.claim: The toggle's accessible name changes between 'Show more' and 'Show less' while it also carries aria-expanded. Screen-reader users get redundant or conflicting state announcements. External links open in a new tab with no indication to assistive technology.
Links without a scheme, such as www.example.com, are not linkified even though owners commonly paste them. This is a gap against the stated goal of making URLs clickable.

truncate and tokenize are tested only through component-level tests in a file named for the component. There are no unit tests in linkify and no tests for paren URLs, unbroken long text, Unicode, or the punctuation-run input that exposes the regex cost.
